\begin{sidewaystable}[ht]
\centering
\scriptsize
\begin{minipage}{21cm}
\caption{Summary of catch allocation strategies used to distribute total catch advice from a single-region estimation model (EM) among regions and fleets. Strategies differ in the degree to which they incorporate recent fishing patterns and spatial signals of abundance. For strategies using empirical catch or survey information, allocation weights were calculated from recent three-year mean catch or survey-index values.}
\label{tab:catch_allocation}
\end{minipage}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}

\begin{tabular}{p{2.5cm} p{2.5cm} p{2.5cm} p{2.5cm} p{5cm} p{6cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Strategy} &
\textbf{Allocation basis} &
\textbf{Regional signal} &
\textbf{Fleet signal} &
\textbf{Equation} &
\textbf{Description} \\
\midrule

Equal &
None &
No &
No &
{\raggedright
\(
C_{r,f} = \frac{C_{\mathrm{total}}}{4}
\)\par} &
Total catch divided equally among all four region-fleet combinations, independent of spatial structure or fleet type. \\

Gear-Equal &
Historical catch &
No &
Yes &
{\raggedright
\(
C_{r,f_g}
=
C_{\mathrm{total}}
\times
\frac{\sum_{r'} C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r',g}}
{\sum_{r',g'} C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r',g'}}
\times
\frac{1}{2}
\)\par} &
Catch first allocated between commercial and recreational fleets according to historical total catches across regions, and then divided equally between regions within each fleet. \\

Fleet-Catch &
Historical catch &
Yes &
Yes &
{\raggedright
\(
C_{r,f}
=
C_{\mathrm{total}}
\times
\frac{C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r,f}}
{\sum_{r',f'} C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r',f'}}
\)\par} &
Catch allocated in proportion to each region-fleet combination's historical share of total catch. \\

Index-Equal &
Survey index &
Yes &
No &
{\raggedright
\(
C_{r,f}
=
C_{\mathrm{total}}
\times
\frac{I^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r}}
{\sum_{r'} I^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r'}}
\times
\frac{1}{2}
\)\par} &
Catch allocated among regions in proportion to historical survey indices, and then divided equally between commercial and recreational fleets within each region. \\

Index-Gear &
Survey index + catch &
Yes &
Yes &
{\raggedright
\(
C_{r,f_g}
=
C_{\mathrm{total}}
\times
\frac{I^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r}}
{\sum_{r'} I^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r'}}
\times
\frac{C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r,g}}
{\sum_{g'} C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r,g'}}
\)\par} &
Catch allocated among regions in proportion to historical survey indices and, within each region, allocated between fleets in proportion to historical catches. \\

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{2mm}
\begin{minipage}{21cm}
\scriptsize \textit{Note:}
$r$ indexes regions ($r=1,2$);
$f$ indexes fleets (commercial and recreational fleets within each region);
$g$ indexes fleet type; the term gear in strategy names refers to commercial and recreational fleet types;
$C_{\mathrm{total}}$ is total catch advice from the estimation model;
$C^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r,f}$ is historical mean catch for region $r$ and fleet $f$;
$I^{\mathrm{hist}}_{r}$ is the historical mean survey index for region $r$.
\end{minipage}
\end{sidewaystable}

\begin{sidewaystable}[ht]
\centering
\scriptsize
\begin{minipage}{23.1cm}
\caption{Summary of performance metrics. Metrics are computed within each simulation realization and then averaged across $N$ retained realizations. Catch and SSB are summarized over short-term and long-term windows, corresponding to the first $k$ years and last $\ell$ years of the feedback period, respectively (here $k=\ell=10$). Average annual variation and risk probabilities are summarized across the full feedback period. Metric scores are min--max scaled across catch allocation strategies within each operating model (OM) scenario and spatial scale, with variability and risk metrics inverted so that higher scores indicate better performance.}
\label{tab:perf_metrics}
\end{minipage}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{p{5.7cm} p{10.6cm} p{6.8cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Performance metric} & \textbf{Equation} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule

Short-term average catch &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{Catch\_ST},m}
=
\frac{1}{k}\sum_{y=1}^{k} C^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}
\) &
Realization-level mean catch over the first $k$ years of the feedback period. \\

Short-term average SSB &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{SSB\_ST},m}
=
\frac{1}{k}\sum_{y=1}^{k} \mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}
\) &
Realization-level mean SSB over the first $k$ years of the feedback period. \\

Long-term average catch &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{Catch\_LT},m}
=
\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{y=n-\ell+1}^{n} C^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}
\) &
Realization-level mean catch over the last $\ell$ years of the feedback period. \\

Long-term average SSB &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{SSB\_LT},m}
=
\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{y=n-\ell+1}^{n} \mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}
\) &
Realization-level mean SSB over the last $\ell$ years of the feedback period. \\

Probability of overfishing $P[\mathrm{OF}]$ &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{POF},m}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{y=1}^{n}
\mathbb{I}\!\left(
\frac{F^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}}{F^{(t)}_{o,r,40\%,y,m}}>1
\right)
\) &
Realization-level proportion of feedback years with $F/F_{40\%}>1$. \\

Probability of being overfished $P[\mathrm{OFD}]$ &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{POFD},m}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{y=1}^{n}
\mathbb{I}\!\left(
\frac{\mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}}
{\mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,40\%,y,m}}<0.5
\right)
\) &
Realization-level proportion of feedback years with $\mathrm{SSB}/\mathrm{SSB}_{40\%}<0.5$. \\

Average annual catch variation &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{AAVC},m}
=
\frac{
\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{y=2}^{n}
\left|C^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}-C^{(t)}_{o,r,y-1,m}\right|}
{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{y=1}^{n} C^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}}
\) &
Realization-level mean absolute annual change in catch, scaled by mean catch across the feedback period. \\

Average annual SSB variation &
\(\displaystyle
\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,\mathrm{AAVS},m}
=
\frac{
\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{y=2}^{n}
\left|\mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}-\mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y-1,m}\right|}
{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{y=1}^{n} \mathrm{SSB}^{(t)}_{o,r,y,m}}
\) &
Realization-level mean absolute annual change in SSB, scaled by mean SSB across the feedback period. \\

\midrule
Aggregated metric value (across realizations) &
\(\displaystyle
x_{o,r,j,m}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{t=1}^{N}\tilde{x}^{(t)}_{o,r,j,m}
\) &
Mean across $N$ retained realizations of the realization-level metric values. \\

Metric score (0--1; ``higher is better'') &
\(\displaystyle
s_{o,r,j,m}=
\frac{x_{o,r,j,m}-\min_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}}
{\max_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}-\min_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}},
\quad s_{o,r,j,m}\in[0,1]
\) &
Min--max scaling for metric $j$ across strategies $m$ within each OM scenario $o$ and spatial scale $r$, when larger values indicate better performance, such as catch or SSB. \\

Metric score (0--1; ``lower is better'') &
\(\displaystyle
s_{o,r,j,m}=
1-
\frac{x_{o,r,j,m}-\min_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}}
{\max_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}-\min_{m'}x_{o,r,j,m'}},
\quad s_{o,r,j,m}\in[0,1]
\) &
Min--max scaling for metric $j$ across strategies $m$ within each OM scenario $o$ and spatial scale $r$, when smaller values indicate better performance, such as variability or risk. \\

Average scaled performance score &
\(\displaystyle
A_{o,r,m}=\frac{1}{J}\sum_{j=1}^{J}s_{o,r,j,m},
\qquad J=8,
\quad A_{o,r,m}\in[0,1]
\) &
Equal-weight descriptive summary across the eight metric scores used in the multi-metric performance figures; values range from 0 to 1. \\

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{2mm}
\begin{minipage}{23.1cm}
\scriptsize \textit{Note:} $o$ indexes OM scenarios; $r$ indexes spatial scale (region 1, region 2, and the system-level aggregate); $m$ indexes catch allocation strategies; $t$ indexes simulation realizations ($t=1,\ldots,N$); $j$ indexes performance metrics; $k$ and $\ell$ denote the short- and long-term windows; $n$ is the number of years in the feedback period; $\mathbb{I}(\cdot)$ is an indicator function. Scores are computed separately for each $(o,r,j)$ by scaling across strategies $m$.
\end{minipage}
\end{sidewaystable}

\clearpage

\begin{sidewaystable}[ht]
\centering
\scriptsize
\begin{minipage}{23cm}
\caption{Summary of empirical allocation strategy tradeoffs, relative performance patterns in the MSE, and management situations for which each strategy may be most appropriate.}
\label{tab:allocation_tradeoffs}
\end{minipage}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{p{2cm} p{4.3cm} p{4.5cm} p{5.7cm} p{6.5cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Strategy} &
\textbf{Information used} &
\textbf{Main advantage} &
\textbf{Main limitation} &
\textbf{Best suited for} \\
\midrule

Equal &
No regional or fleet information &
Transparent, stable, and low data demand. &
Could not respond to directional movement or regional productivity decline, increasing localized depletion risk in vulnerable components. &
Situations where regional productivity and depletion risk are expected to be similar, or where transparency and catch stability are primary objectives. \\

Gear-Equal &
Historical fleet catch shares; equal regional split within each fleet &
Produced stable catch outcomes while preserving broad fleet allocation patterns. &
Lacked regional biological information, so regional risk could remain hidden when movement or productivity differed among regions. &
Situations where maintaining broad fleet continuity is important and persistent regional differences in productivity or risk are not expected to dominate. \\

Fleet-Catch &
Recent $x$-year mean region-fleet catch shares &
Incorporated recent fishing patterns, fleet access, and spatial catch distribution; provided an intermediate level of variability. &
Catch reflected regulations, profitability, access, reporting, and historical fishing patterns as well as biomass, so allocation could lag biological change or regional productivity shifts. &
Situations where recent catch is expected to reasonably reflect resource availability, fleet access, and spatial fishing opportunities. \\

Index-Equal &
Recent $x$-year mean regional survey indices; equal fleet split within each region &
Responded directly to regional abundance signals and could reduce localized depletion risk when survey signals tracked regional risk. &
Increased interannual catch variability; survey indices could reflect seasonal availability rather than annual exploitable biomass or spawning contribution. &
Situations where regional survey indices reliably track relative abundance or depletion risk and managers can tolerate greater catch variability. \\

Index-Gear &
Recent $x$-year mean regional survey indices plus fleet catch shares within each region &
Combined a regional abundance signal with fleet allocation history. &
Shared the survey-timing and variability concerns of Index-Equal while also depending on catch shares within regions. &
Situations where regional survey responsiveness is desired, but fleet-specific catch history and access also need to be retained. \\

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{2mm}
\begin{minipage}{23cm}
\scriptsize \textit{Note:}
$x$ is the smoothing window used to calculate recent empirical catch or survey-index allocation weights; in this study, $x=3$ years.
\end{minipage}
\end{sidewaystable}

\clearpage

\setcounter{table}{0}
\renewcommand{\thetable}{S\arabic{table}}

\begin{sidewaystable}[ht]
\centering
\small
\begin{minipage}{22.9cm}
\caption{Summary of movement and recruitment formulations used in operating model scenarios. Scenario abbreviations denote combinations of population structure and process representation: N = natal homing, M = metapopulation; B = bidirectional, U = unidirectional movement; L = low movement magnitude; H = high movement magnitude; I = IID interannual movement, O = ontogenetic movement; D = declining recruitment in population component 1; BH = density-dependent Beverton--Holt recruitment.}
\label{tab:OM_formulations}
\end{minipage}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.35}
\begin{tabular}{p{2.9cm} p{3.2cm} p{7.6cm} p{9.2cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Scenario(s)} &
\textbf{Process} &
\textbf{Equation} &
\textbf{Description} \\
\midrule

NBLI, MBLI &
IID$_y$ movement &
\(\displaystyle
\begin{aligned}
\text{logit}(m_{i,a,r\to r',y}) &=
\text{logit}(\bar m_{i,a,r\to r'}) + \delta_{i,r\to r',y},\\
\delta_{i,r\to r',y} &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\text{move}}^2),
\qquad \sigma_{\text{move}}=0.5
\end{aligned}
\)
&
Mean movement rates vary stochastically among years via IID random effects on the logit scale. Directionality constraints (bidirectional or unidirectional) are enforced by fixing prohibited transitions to zero. \\
\midrule

NBLO, MBLO &
Ontogenetic movement &
\(\displaystyle
m_{i,a,r\to r'}
=
\frac{m^{\max}_{i,r\to r'}}{1 + \exp\!\left[-k(a-a_{50})\right]}
\)
&
Movement probability increases systematically with age following a logistic function, representing ontogenetic dispersal behavior. Parameters are $k = 2$ (steepness) and $a_{50} = 1$ (age at which 50\% of maximum movement is reached). \\
\midrule

NBLD, NULD &
Declining recruitment &
\(\displaystyle
\log(R_{1,y})
=
\log(\bar R_{1,0})
-
d_R(y-y_0)
+
\varepsilon^R_{1,y},
\;
\varepsilon^R_{1,y}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_R^2),
\;
\ d_R=0.016\ \text{yr}^{-1},
\;
\sigma_R=0.75
\)
&
Recruitment varies stochastically around a declining time-varying mean. For population component~1, mean recruitment declines at a fixed rate of $0.016$ yr$^{-1}$ in log space during the feedback period, representing a cumulative 0.8 reduction in log recruitment over 50 years. Population component~2 remains stationary around its mean recruitment. \\
\midrule

NBH-BH, MBH-BH &
Density-dependent recruitment &
\(\displaystyle
\bar R_{i,y} =
\frac{\alpha_i\,SSB_{i,y}}{1+\beta_i\,SSB_{i,y}},
\qquad
\log(R_{i,y})=
\log(\bar R_{i,y})+\varepsilon^R_{i,y},
\;
\varepsilon^R_{i,y}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_R^2),
\;
\sigma_R=0.75
\)
&
Mean recruitment follows a Beverton--Holt stock--recruitment relationship with lognormal deviations. Parameters are $(\alpha_1,\beta_1)=(4.5,10^{-4})$ and $(\alpha_2,\beta_2)=(4.0,10^{-4})$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{sidewaystable}

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\begin{minipage}{15.6cm}
\caption{Summary of model features estimated, fixed, or derived in the single-region estimation model (EM).}
\label{tab:EM_features}
\end{minipage}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{p{5.0cm} p{3.8cm} p{6.8cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model component} & \textbf{Treatment in EM} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
Spatial structure & Fixed & Single-region; no explicit regions, movement, or population components. \\
Mean recruitment & Estimated & Aggregate mean. \\
Recruitment deviation SD & Estimated & IID lognormal recruitment deviations. \\
Numbers-at-age 2+ deviation SD & Estimated & IID lognormal age-2+ deviations. \\
Initial numbers-at-age & Equilibrium initialization & WHAM equilibrium approach. \\
Annual fishing mortality by fleet & Estimated & Commercial and recreational fleets. \\
Commercial selectivity & Partly estimated & Ages 1--3 estimated; ages 4--8 fixed at 1. \\
Recreational selectivity & Partly estimated & Ages 1--4 estimated; ages 5--8 fixed at 1. \\
Survey selectivity & Partly estimated & Age 1 estimated; ages 2--8 fixed at 1. \\
Survey catchability & Estimated & Aggregate survey index. \\
Catch observation error CVs & Fixed & Commercial = 0.05; recreational = 0.15. \\
Survey-index observation error CV & Fixed & CV = 0.4. \\
Age-composition ESS & Fixed & ESS = 50. \\
Natural mortality ($M$) & Fixed & 0.4 for all ages. \\
Weight-at-age & Fixed inputs & Aggregated before fitting EM. \\
Maturity-at-age & Fixed inputs & Aggregated before fitting EM. \\
$F_{40\%}$ & Derived & Calculated from each EM fit. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
